The page gives no area; the provinces it lists for the maximum extent (Toledo, Ciudad Real, Cuenca, northern Albacete, Cáceres, Guadalajara, Madrid) are consistent with the 77,000 km2 shape, so no area objection.

correction.text: unchanged from 1018 (the page: 'In 1018, Ismail expelled the governor of the city of Toledo, establishing a de facto independence')

keyframe_review.note: Same shape (77,316 km2); drawn as the taifa from 1018 only, '1015-1017' is Caliphate land. The page's largest extent (provinces of Toledo, Ciudad Real, Cuenca, northern Albacete, Cáceres, Guadalajara, Madrid) is not dated, so the shape stands for 1018-1033.
77,536 km2, no change in the record: the page dates no gain or loss between 1018 and 1062. 'Already by 1036, Ismail al-Zahir appears as sovereign king of the taifa.'
77,681 km2. The page dates nothing for 1040-1045; Ismail al-Zahir held the throne to 1043 'fighting for his independence against Córdoba', then al-Ma'mun 1043-1075.

77,536 km2 for 1046-1065. In 1062 Ferdinand I took Talamanca and besieged Alcalá de Henares, and al-Ma'mun paid parias (ledger); the Ferdinand I page does not say Talamanca stayed Castilian, so the shape stands.

correction.text: the 1066 shape, drawn from 1065; Valencia 'absorbed into the Taifa of Toledo' 1065-1085 (Valencia page, territory by stage)

The Valencia page says 'Al-Ma'mun of Toledo seized Valencia, annexing it to the Taifa of Toledo' in 1065 (key dates 'annexed by Toledo 1065'); the Toledo page says 'to annex Valencia (1064)'. Draw the larger shape from 1065.

90,279 km2 for 1072-1084. Three episodes the shape does not show are in the ledger: Córdoba held 1075-1077 (new keyframe taifa-of-toledo_1075), Toledo under Badajoz 1080-1081, and Valencia 'slipping from Toledo's control' after 1075 (Valencia page; kept in the shape until 1085 because 'Absorbed into the Taifa of Toledo 1065-1085' is the page's own stage summary).

The extent of the taifa of Córdoba is taken as the province of Córdoba (12,900 km2), the page naming no boundary. The Córdoba page says only that Toledo's emir besieged the city and that Seville lost it 1075-1078.

correction.text: 1085 only: the Toledan lands without Valencia, until 6 May 1085 when 'Toledo officially and peacefully fell into Christian hands'

keyframe_review.note: 47,127 km2 for 1085-1093 has no support: the taifa ends in 1085 ('Disestablished: 1085', 'Toledo officially and peacefully fell into Christian hands on 6 May 1085'; Alfonso VI's page 'finally fell on 25 May 1085') and its successor is the Kingdom of Toledo within Castile. For 1085 only, draw the 1072 shape minus the Valencia core, which was a separate Castilian-vassal kingdom under al-Qadir from March 1086 (Valencia page, 'Alfonso installed al-Qadir in Valencia as his vassal'); from 1086 the land is Castilian.

region.text: Toledo and its district; the page: 'It emerged after 1018 upon the fracturing of the Caliphate of Córdoba'

ledger.note: 1018: Toledo breaks away from the Caliphate of Córdoba. 'In 1018, Ismail expelled the governor of the city of Toledo, establishing a de facto independence' (infobox 'Established: 1018 (de facto)'); the page names the city, not a boundary, so the core is Cliopatria's shape.

region.text: the east of al-Mamun's taifa: Talamanca and Alcalá de Henares

ledger.note: 1062: Ferdinand I invades the east of Toledo's taifa. 'In 1062, Ferdinand invaded the east of al-Mamun's taifa, taking Talamanca and besieging Alcalá de Henares.'

region.text: Talamanca and Alcalá de Henares, left when the parias were agreed

ledger.note: 1062: al-Ma'mun buys Ferdinand off. 'After seeing his country plundered, al-Mamun agreed to pay parias and Ferdinand left.' Toledo becomes a tributary of León-Castile (the Castile dossier should carry the vassal_start with counterpart taifa-of-toledo; Alfonso VI's page: 'In 1074, he probably recovered payment of the parias of Toledo'). The page does not say whether Talamanca was kept.

region.text: Valencia and its surrounding area, 'one of the major urban centres of al-Andalus'

ledger.note: 1065: al-Ma'mun annexes Valencia. 'Al-Ma'mun of Toledo seized Valencia, annexing it to the Taifa of Toledo, and installed his vizier as governor'; the Toledo page says 'to annex Valencia (1064)' after Ferdinand's 1061 attack on its ruler. Cliopatria's Toledo shape grows in 1066 by exactly the Valencia core.

region.text: the Cordoban lands, the taifa of Córdoba held by Seville since 1070

ledger.note: 1075: Toledo conquers the taifa of Córdoba. 'helped Al-Mamun of Toledo in conquering the taifa of Córdoba in 1075.' The Córdoba page does not say Toledo took the city: it says the Emir of Toledo besieged it and that 'Seville lost control of Córdoba from 1075 to 1078'; Seville had captured it in 1070.

1077: the Cordoban lands are lost. 'The Cordoban lands were lost in 1077.' The Toledo page does not name the taker; the Córdoba page implies Seville regained the city, dating its loss of control 1075-1078, so the counterpart is the Córdoba page's reading.

region.text: the taifa of Toledo, 'incorporated into the taifa of Badajoz' 1080-1081

ledger.note: 1080: al-Mutawakkil of Badajoz occupies Toledo. 'Al-Mutawakkil occupied Toledo in 1080' and the infobox has 'Incorporated into the taifa of Badajoz: 1080-1081'; the page names the city, the extent is the whole taifa by the infobox's word 'incorporated'.

region.text: the taifa of Toledo restored under Yahya al-Qadir

ledger.note: 1081: Yahya al-Qadir regains Toledo. 'He was able to regain the throne the following year'; the page's list has 'restored 1081-1085'.

1085: Valencia is no longer held from Toledo. The pages are silent on a date: the Valencia page says Valencia 'began slipping from Toledo's control' after 1075 and gives 'Absorbed into the Taifa of Toledo' 1065-1085; Alfonso VI installed al-Qadir there as king in early March 1086. Cliopatria's Valencia shape resumes in 1085. Bridging judgment.

region.text: the whole taifa, 'Succeeded by: Kingdom of Toledo (Crown of Castile)'; without Valencia, lost before the fall (ledger 1085 loss to taifa-of-valencia; keyframe taifa-of-toledo_1085)

ledger.note: 1085: Alfonso VI takes Toledo. 'Toledo officially and peacefully fell into Christian hands on 6 May 1085' (infobox 'Disestablished: 1085'); Alfonso VI's page has 'Toledo, which finally fell on 25 May 1085' and that he 'proclaimed himself victoriosissimo rege in Toleto'. The land becomes the Kingdom of Toledo within Castile.

wars.name: Ferdinand I's invasion of the taifa of Toledo
wars.outcome: Ferdinand took Talamanca, besieged Alcalá de Henares and left when al-Ma'mun agreed to pay parias.
wars.note: The page also dates Ferdinand's 'great raid' on Seville and Badajoz to 1063 and the parias of Zaragoza to 1060; neither moved Toledo's border.

wars.name: Toledan annexation of Valencia
wars.outcome: Al-Ma'mun seized Valencia and installed his vizier as governor; Ferdinand I's own siege of Valencia in 1065 failed ('did not have the forces to take the city').
wars.note: The Toledo page dates the annexation 1064, the Valencia page 1065; the Ferdinand I page gives the attack on Valencia as 1065.

wars.name: Toledo and Seville over Córdoba
wars.outcome: Seville took Córdoba in 1070 after defeating the Toledan army; Toledo held the Cordoban lands 1075-1077; Seville regained them by 1078.
wars.note: Toledo page: conquest 1075, lost 1077. Córdoba page: Seville lost control 1075-1078.

wars.name: Conquest of Toledo
wars.outcome: Toledo surrendered to Alfonso VI in May 1085 and became the Kingdom of Toledo within Castile; al-Qadir was sent to Valencia.
wars.note: Alfonso VI's page does not say when the siege began (the Taifa page has no siege either), so the 1084 start is Cliopatria's last shape year, not a page date.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given for any frontier of the taifa; the Castilian frontier was approximate, and the pages date no boundary except the places named in 1062.

notes:
IDENTITY. The Taifa page dates independence to 1018 ('Established: 1018 (de facto)'), eight years after Cliopatria's first row (1010); the dossier starts in 1018 and the 1010 and 1015 shapes are adjusted to 1018. The page's ruler list starts c. 1036 (Ismail al-Zahir), so the ruler strip has nothing for 1018-1035. The end is 1085 (6 May on the Taifa page, 25 May on Alfonso VI's page).
CLIOPATRIA. Shape 1066 (+Valencia core) is one year late against the Valencia page (1065) and two against the Toledo page (1064). Shape 1085-1093 (47,127 km2) is unsupported: the taifa ended in 1085 and the land is Castilian. The Taifa page gives no area, so no area comparison could be made.
UNSETTLED. (1) The parias: Toledo paid Ferdinand I from 1062 (Ferdinand I page) and Alfonso VI 'probably recovered payment' in 1074; the Castile dossier should hold the vassal_start (counterpart taifa-of-toledo), no vassal event is written here because the schema gives the counterpart as the vassal itself. (2) Who held Córdoba in 1075-1077 and 1077-1078: the Toledo page and the Córdoba page differ (see the ledger); Seville is used as counterpart on the Córdoba page's reading. (3) The 1080-1081 Badajoz interlude is a loss and a regain of the whole taifa; the Badajoz dossier should carry the mirror events. (4) When Valencia left Toledo's control is not dated by any page opened (ledger event at confidence 1). (5) The Ismail al-Zahir dating: the page has 1018 for the expulsion of the governor and 'around 1035' for Ismail's arrival.
GAZETTEER. Alcalá de Henares and Talamanca (de Jarama) are not in places.jsonl; a coordinate radius is used.
PAGES. Five opened (Taifa of Toledo, Taifa of Valencia, Ferdinand I of León, Alfonso VI of León and Castile, Taifa of Córdoba); no page failed.
